13 Nov 2026Tsinghua University; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences; Binzhou Institute of Technology

Machine-learned potentials resolve a disorder trade-off in lithium cathode transport

Using actively fine-tuned machine-learning interatomic potentials with experimental validation, the authors report that cation disorder improves lithium-path connectivity but broadens site energies, suppressing diffusion in disordered-rocksalt cathodes. They develop an energy-adjusted percolation descriptor and a Li–Mn–Ti–O design map. This is a composition-specific transport result; the review does not assign individual capacity figures to modeled or measured material states.

Technology: Actively fine-tuned machine-learning interatomic potentials

13 Nov 2026IBM Research; Cleveland Clinic; Cleveland Clinic Lerner College of Medicine of Case Western Reserve University

Foundation model and generative AI yield 3CL protease inhibitors confirmed at sub-micromolar IC50

An AI-assisted 3CL-protease inhibitor study selected 249 molecules from about five million generated candidates and evaluated 18 using free-energy perturbation. Five molecules were experimentally tested; all five inhibited the target below 1 micromolar IC50, and one inhibited more strongly than its lead. MMELON activity predictions had Pearson R=0.72 in a blind test. This summary is limited to the abstract and November 13, 2026 publication metadata; it does not establish antiviral efficacy in people.

Technology: MMELON biomedical foundation model with generative molecular models

The paper was published November 10; this entry represents the November 13 announcement.

Technology: Human-in-the-loop AI copilot with topology optimization (machine-learning region-flagging model)

13 Nov 2026Imperial College London; University of Antwerp and Antwerp University Hospital; Maastricht University Medical Center; Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center; Zhongshan Hospital of Fudan University

AI-enhanced electrocardiography for detection and prediction of dilated cardiomyopathy

In the journal abstract, an AI-ECG model trained on more than 330,000 ECG–echocardiogram pairs detected the dilated-cardiomyopathy phenotype (AUROC 0.87–0.97) and predicted later disease (C-index 0.80–0.87). In familial cohorts, five-year negative predictive values were 95.5% in Antwerp and 91.5% in Maastricht; positive predictive values were 42.4% and 39.4%. These are diagnostic and risk-prediction findings, not demonstrated clinical benefit.

Technology: Explainable deep learning model applied to electrocardiography

13 Nov 2026Stanford University

Antibody design across observed and forecasted antigenic evolution

The Germinal Multi preprint abstract reports antibodies designed against several antigen variants at once. Experimental screens of tens of designs per campaign found binders to resistance-associated EGFR variants and neutralizers of historical SARS-CoV-2 variants, including variants withheld from design. Redesign of BD55-1205 restored neutralization of a forecast-guided engineered escape variant while retaining parental-variant activity. The escape result concerns an engineered variant, not a demonstrated future circulating strain. Review is limited to the abstract and original-server metadata.

Technology: Germinal Multi (computational antibody design framework); evolutionary forecasting model

12 Nov 2026MIT; Imperial College London

Unrealistic emissions scenarios help AI climate models prepare for unfamiliar futures

MIT researchers with Imperial College London designed a small synthetic set of deliberately unrealistic emissions scenarios to train climate emulators, which normally need six to eight full Earth system model runs that each take months. The method needs only one model run, and the emulator predicted unseen scenarios and local pollutant-control effects where traditional emulators failed. It was validated with a simple climate model rather than a full Earth system model, and the article reports no quantitative accuracy metrics.

Technology: Climate emulator trained on optimized synthetic scenarios

12 Nov 2026Christopher D. Rosin (Constructive Codes; independent research project)

GPT-6 Astra constructs mutually orthogonal Latin squares that improve lower bounds at 33 orders

GPT-6 Astra produced explicit mutually orthogonal Latin-square constructions that improve known lower bounds for N(n) at 33 values of n from 22 through 494. The standout construction gives four MOLS of order 22, completing the last open case needed to show N(n)≥4 for every n>10. The same paper reports resulting bounds at other orders and derives a strongly regular graph with parameters (484,126,40,30) from the order-22 construction; these connected consequences are counted once as one paper-level result.

Technology: OpenAI GPT-6 Astra, used through ChatGPT Pro and the OpenAI Codex harness

t-SNE-selected LMC radio source receives a spectroscopic AGN classification at z = 2.80

SALT spectroscopy of the previously unclassified source LMC tSNE b8 (R.A. 06:22:41.86, Dec. −68:59:21.9) identified it as an active galactic nucleus at redshift z = 2.80. The source was selected from the blazar-like sequence in a t-SNE map combining VISTA near-infrared and ASKAP radio survey data with multi-wavelength photometry. This is one specific spectroscopic classification from the paper’s broader follow-up sample.

Technology: t-distributed stochastic neighbour embedding (t-SNE) applied to multi-wavelength source photometry

11 Nov 2026CSIRO; The University of Western Australia

GenDIReCT recovers the M87* ring from archival telescope data

GenDIReCT used diffusion-based reconstruction conditioned on calibration-independent closure invariants to analyze EHT observations from 2017, 2018 and 2021. The authors recover ring morphology and estimate a diameter of 42.2 ± 1.5 microarcseconds; geometric modeling gives 42.3 ± 1.1. This is a new analysis of existing observations, overlapping the target and some data of the cataloged 2023 PRIMO reconstruction. It is not a new observation or the first black-hole-shadow discovery.

Technology: GenDIReCT latent diffusion

11 Nov 2026Google Research

Wearable-based health age models for cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic risk profiling and coaching

Google Research reported a wearable-based health-age model associated with subsequent hypertension, cardiovascular disease and type 2 diabetes in the All of Us cohort (22,748 participants). A companion world model simulated 12-week trajectories. In 490 blinded paired reviews, coaches preferred simulation-grounded plans in 71.4% of evaluations; physicians rated 97.6% of physiological claims accurate. This summary is limited to the November 11, 2026 institutional blog. The authors state all evaluations were offline and retrospective; clinical effectiveness and durable habit change require prospective trials.

Technology: Coachable health-age model, SensorWM action-conditioned world model, feasibility-constrained optimizer with a language model agent, multimodal CKM deviation model

9 Nov 2026Harvard Medical School; Harvard College; New York Genome Center; Rush Alzheimer’s Disease Center, Rush University

TriSCOPE links cell-type-specific Alzheimer’s expression programs to inherited risk loci

TriSCOPE combined cell-level predictive modeling, donor-aware differential expression and pseudotime analysis across six single-nucleus RNA-sequencing datasets (about 4.2 million nuclei from 627 donors). It identified cell-type-specific predictively expressed genes that were often missed by univariate differential-expression analysis; conditional GWAS–eQTL colocalization supported 27 gene–cell-type pairs at Alzheimer’s risk loci, including pairs without significant differential expression. Selected gene signals and analytical branches were compared across independent cohorts.

Technology: TriSCOPE, using LightGBM-based multivariate predictive modeling integrated with differential expression and pseudotime analysis

Relevance 60 physics Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

Result, AI contribution and limits

Evidence context (descriptions follow the cited sources; test type is a catalog classification):

  • Publication status: Peer-reviewed paper
  • Test type: direct test
  • Tested: Subaru/MOIRCS spectroscopy of four PCFNet-selected candidate regions confirmed four protoclusters at z = 3.316, 3.403, 3.408 and 3.425, across three regions, with galaxy-density peaks more than five times the uniform distribution.
  • Still unknown: This is a small follow-up sample: four of 121 PCFNet candidates were targeted, and the parent catalogue is trained on simulated galaxies. Four protoclusters are confirmed across three of four observed regions; a fourth observed candidate region had no significant redshift peak. One of the confirmed regions had previously been reported as a photometric candidate, so this is a spectroscopic confirmation/characterization result rather than four wholly unprecedented structures. The halo masses are inferred from member stellar masses, not direct lensing measurements. The elevated SFR densities depend on membership-probability weighting and are sensitive to assumed geometry, volume and methodology. Metallicity excesses are only 1.4–2 sigma in two systems; two others are statistically consistent with the field. The authors’ proposed gas-inflow/recycling explanation is interpretive.
  • AI role: PCFNet used broad-band optical photometry and galaxy positions to assign protocluster-membership probabilities and identify candidate regions. The model outputs determined which regions received Subaru/MOIRCS follow-up and prioritized slit targets; their probabilities also informed member selection and the authors’ volume/SFR-density estimator. Spectroscopy then tested those predictions, finding a 40% member detection rate among high-probability galaxies and confirming three of four observed regions.

Evidence sources: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.35471

Deep-learning denoising reveals new short-period seismic observations of known ultra-low-velocity zones

A supervised deep-learning denoising autoencoder exposed previously undocumented short-period S-diffracted wave observations associated with several known ultra-low-velocity zones (ULVZs). It also revealed four Hawaiian-ULVZ S-diff post-cursor records at Japan F-net stations from East Pacific Rise earthquakes, providing ray paths with mean azimuth about 78° from earlier North American paths. These new cross-cutting observations add constraints on ULVZ geometry and frequency/azimuth-dependent waveforms, but the paper does not present a new ULVZ detection or a completed structural inversion.

  • Still unknown: This paper reports new seismic observations sampling known ULVZs; it does not establish a new ULVZ structure. The Japanese post-cursors are difficult to separate from the main S-diff phases and require future 3D modelling to determine their interpretation and resolve trade-offs. Denoiser amplitude fidelity is a limitation, especially under training/application mismatch; the authors advise caution for single-station denoising. These are observational constraints, not a completed inversion of shape or composition.
  • AI role: The denoiser was trained on synthetic seismic waveforms mixed with real global noise, then used to separate signal from noise in real S-diff record sections. Its output helped researchers identify short-period post-cursor observations not reported in earlier literature, including four events recorded in Japan with nearly perpendicular ray geometry to previous North American observations of the Hawaiian ULVZ.

Symbolic regression derives aircraft aerodynamic scaling across sharp-cone and blunt-body geometries

A Chain of Symbolic Regression (CoSR) analysis of hypersonic simulation data derived an interpretable non-power-product scaling relation for axial-force coefficient across sharp-cone and blunt-body configurations. It combines angle of attack, Mach number and Reynolds number through a dominant term and a viscous correction; the relation has a shared functional form but geometry-specific fitted constants. The authors interpret the constants as reflecting differences in shock/base drag, friction drag and pressure drag. This is a new model-derived scaling result from simulations, not a wind-tunnel or flight measurement.

The simpler dominant component is linked to known hypersonic invariance, while the learned viscous correction and geometry-specific scaling provide the paper’s new modeled relationship. Do not treat the authors’ drag-component interpretations as direct measurements.
  • AI role: CoSR progressively searched for interpretable dimensionless groups and combined their relationships instead of fitting one end-to-end expression. Applied to hypersonic simulation data, it identified a dominant angle-of-attack/Mach term and a Reynolds-number-dependent viscous correction, then fitted geometry-specific constants for two body shapes. Earlier canonical-law and fluid examples in the same paper are framework validations and are not counted separately here.

Evidence sources: https://journals.aps.org/prresearch/abstract/10.1103/f2kp-pp4q

LHCb reports first single-experiment evidence for B⁰ → μ⁺μ⁻ decay

Using 18 fb⁻¹ of Run 3 data and earlier LHCb data, the collaboration reports first single-experiment evidence for the rare B⁰→μ⁺μ⁻ decay, with a combined significance of 3.2σ and measured branching fraction (1.14 +0.42/−0.39 stat. +0.06/−0.05 syst.)×10⁻¹⁰. 29 Oct 2026University of Cambridge; California Institute of Technology

GPT-6 Astra resolves the spectral isometry conjecture for arbitrary unital C*-algebras

The paper proves that every unital surjective complex-linear spectral isometry between unital C*-algebras is a Jordan isomorphism; without unitality, such a map is a central-unitary multiple of a Jordan isomorphism. The proof establishes that entire one-parameter groups of unital spectral isometries are algebra automorphisms, then reduces the general case to the commutative case. The authors report that the result was formally verified in Lean.

Technology: OpenAI GPT-6 Astra

9 Oct 2026Yu Chen; and Yiting Wang (affiliations not specified in arXiv record)

GPT-6 Pro proves a quadratic-size threshold suffices for random permutations to contain every length-n pattern

The paper proves that a uniformly random permutation of length 32n² contains every permutation of length n as a pattern with probability at least 1−exp(−c n/log n), for an absolute c>0 and sufficiently large n. This removes the prior log-log factor from the sufficient-length bound, resolves Alon’s open 1000n² problem, and establishes the correct Θ(n²) order.

8 Oct 2026ATLAS Collaboration; CERN

ATLAS graph neural network enables first LHC observation of single-top s-channel production

Using 140 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV proton–proton collisions, ATLAS reports the first observation of single-top-quark s-channel production at the LHC, with 5.1σ observed (5.2σ expected) significance. The measured cross-section is 10.8 ± 1.5(stat) ± 1.6(syst) pb, consistent with the Standard Model. A graph neural network discriminant separates the signal from top-pair, W+jets and t-channel single-top backgrounds; the analysis also uses broadened event acceptance, improved b tagging and refined modeling.

  • AI role: Craig supplied the refinement strategy; Astra developed key construction steps, led proof development and carried out proposed verification work.

5 Oct 2026The University of Tokyo; Los Alamos National Laboratory

Recurrent neural network reveals near-critical seeding of topological defects in Kibble–Zurek simulations

In numerical simulations of a one-dimensional Landau–Ginzburg phase transition, a recurrent neural network predicted the final locations of topological defects from short sequences of order-parameter fluctuations during the Kibble–Zurek impulse regime, before freeze-out and before the defects were macroscopically visible. Prediction error across quench rates followed power-law scaling consistent with the Kibble–Zurek freeze-out time, indicating that information about the eventual defect pattern is encoded in near-critical fluctuations in this model.

Technology: Recurrent neural network (RNN); LSTM and Transformer architectures were also checked

Relevance 47 physics Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

Result, AI contribution and limits

Evidence context (descriptions follow the cited sources; test type is a catalog classification):

  • Publication status: Peer-reviewed paper
  • Test type: retrospective or benchmark
  • Tested: In numerical simulations of a one-dimensional Landau–Ginzburg phase transition, a recurrent neural network predicted the final locations of topological defects from short sequences of order-parameter fluctuations during the Kibble–Zurek impulse regime, before freeze-out and before the defects were macroscopically visible.
  • Still unknown: This is a computational result from a noisy one-dimensional Landau–Ginzburg model, not an experimental observation of defects in a material or cosmological system. The paper uses overdamped dynamics (η=1), low noise temperature θ=10⁻⁸, a finite periodic grid and simulated training/test samples; similar behavior at another noise setting is reported in supplementary material. The finding is consistent with the Kibble–Zurek mechanism and an earlier deconstruction of its dynamics; it does not establish that this prediction method applies unchanged to all phase transitions. The PRL article was published 2026-10-05; the original arXiv preprint was submitted 2025-08-28 and revised as v2 on 2026-09-10.
  • AI role: The RNN analyzed short time sequences from numerical order-parameter dynamics and inferred the final kink count and positions from small fluctuations during the impulse regime. This allowed the authors to identify when information about future defect positions becomes predictable, a quantity not directly provided by conventional Kibble–Zurek defect-density scaling. They report similar prediction behavior with LSTM and Transformer models, suggesting the result is not specific to one architecture.

Evidence sources: https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/fstv-lsvh

GPT-6 Astra proves a linear coloring bound for graphs excluding clique minors

The authors present a proof of the Linear Hadwiger conjecture: there is a constant C such that every graph with no K_t minor is colorable with at most Ct colors.   • AI role: An ensemble of a Transformer (R-SMILES 2) predicting precursors and a graph neural network (NeuralLoc) selecting templates, combined by a learned rank-dependent vote.

18 Sep 2026LHCb Collaboration; CERN

LHCb observes the doubly charmed Ωcc⁺ baryon with an 8.7σ global significance

Using 6.3 fb⁻¹ of 13.6 TeV proton-proton collisions recorded in 2024, LHCb observed an Ωc⁰π⁺ mass peak with 8.7σ global significance and identified it as the weakly decaying doubly charmed Ωcc⁺ baryon. The reported mass is 3725.9 ± 1.0 (stat) ± 0.2 (syst) ± 0.4 (lifetime) ± 0.6 (external) MeV/c². A boosted decision tree suppressed random-track combinatorial background; the result is a preprint submitted to Physical Review Letters.

Technology: Boosted decision tree classifier (TMVA toolkit)

17 Sep 2026Xinglong Wu (author affiliation not stated in the arXiv record)

GPT-5.6 constructs a counterexample to Talagrand’s operator cotype problem

The paper gives a negative answer, already for q=2, to Talagrand’s question whether an operator’s Rademacher cotype is universally bounded by its Gaussian cotype and its (q,1)-summing norm. For every sufficiently large power-of-two dimension it constructs a Banach space and operator violating such a universal bound. The same construction also yields a negative answer to Kwapień’s decomposition problem.

15 Sep 2026OpenAI FrontierMath Erdős project; exposition by David R. Wood (affiliation not stated in arXiv record)

GPT-6 Astra finds a counting proof of the Erdős–Sós tree-embedding conjecture

A counting argument proves that every finite graph with average degree greater than t−2 contains every tree on t vertices, resolving the Erdős–Sós conjecture. The proof counts adjacency-marked vertex orderings and uses an induction on the tree to bound those not supporting a rooted copy. The exposition states the sharp classical theorem and records its proof was discovered by GPT-6 Astra; a Lean repository checks the benchmark formalization of the result. Related expository papers of the same proof are aliases, not separate discoveries.

Technology: Pre-release OpenAI GPT-6 Astra in the FrontierMath Erdős benchmark

AI-discovered construction improves the lower bound for the complex Grothendieck constant

The authors prove the classical complex Grothendieck constant exceeds 1.35584631827168, closing more than one quarter of the gap between Davie’s lower bound and Haagerup’s upper bound reported in the paper. The numerical search used Hermite projections and a radial weight; interval arithmetic on exact rational inputs rigorously verifies the stated bound. The authors credit the Odin Automatic AI Research Agent with discovering both the lower bound and its proof.

GPT-5.6 helps prove an exact mapping between frustrated and field-driven spin chains

A single-author preprint proves that every finite one-dimensional open O(n) spin chain with arbitrary inhomogeneous nearest- and next-nearest-neighbor interactions has an exact, temperature-independent Hamiltonian mapping to a simpler nearest-neighbor chain with axial single-spin potentials. A parallel result for q-state Potts chains yields a closed-form solution for every q ≥ 2 and finite chain length. The theorem generalizes a 1990 Heisenberg-chain challenge and connects spontaneous collective behavior from competing interactions to field-induced behavior.

Technology: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol; GPT-5.6 Sol Pro for final adversarial manuscript review

  • Tested: MACE-MP-0b2 interatomic-potential calculations screened 462 four- and five-cation trivalent-oxide compositions and selected 16 for synthesis.

Only three of 16 tested compositions formed phase-pure corundum high-entropy oxides; most attempts produced competing phases, and rhodium-containing samples showed redox instability. Synthesis outcomes depended strongly on route: the three corundum HEOs were phase-pure only with one of solid-state or combustion synthesis. The authors combined these with a stability metric to rank 16 synthesis candidates. Experimental powder-X-ray diffraction and Rietveld refinement then assessed the predicted materials, linking model-guided selection to the new synthesized compositions.

Data-driven equations reveal rainfall-linked North Atlantic decadal variability

Using SINDy equation discovery on monthly observational indices from 1950–2022, researchers derived three linked low-order equations for Atlantic Multidecadal Variability, the North Atlantic Oscillation and North Atlantic precipitation.   • Still unknown: The ATLAS paper was submitted to PRL as a preprint on 2026-07-14; the cited official ATLAS briefing is dated 2026-08-04. The measured fractions agree with the Standard Model; the statistical uncertainty dominates and polarization-template modeling is the leading systematic uncertainty. This is an experimental observation from ATLAS data, not evidence of physics beyond the Standard Model.

Result, AI contribution and limits

Evidence context (descriptions follow the cited sources; test type is a catalog classification):

  • AI role: The authors trained predictive models on phenotypic screening data from >11,000 compounds, then used their scores as rewards/objectives in a generative workflow to propose molecules intended to kill one pancreatic-cancer cell line while sparing another or control cells. Candidate molecules or close purchasable analogues were experimentally tested and dose-response validated.

12 May 2026ETH Zurich; Weizmann Institute of Science; University Children’s Hospital Zurich and University of Zurich

Machine-learning metabolomics identifies widespread promiscuous activities in Escherichia coli enzymes

In vitro metabolomics of 667 purified E. coli enzymes, analyzed with a machine-learning-derived multivariate classifier, indicated previously unrecognized promiscuous activities in 11% of enzymes tested. Follow-up reconstruction assigned 22 reaction stoichiometries to 11 enzymes, with four reactions experimentally validated; examples include expanded nucleotide-substrate use by DeoA, cofactor and sugar promiscuity in NanK, and FMN dephosphorylation by CobC. Follow-up assays also found that pyrimidine-specific ribonucleoside hydrolase RihB acted on thymidine, guanosine and deoxyuridine, further extending its measured substrate range.

Technology: Machine-learning-derived multivariate classifier applied to enzyme metabolomics ion-trace data

Relevance 60 biology Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

Result, AI contribution and limits

Evidence context (descriptions follow the cited sources; test type is a catalog classification):

  • Publication status: Peer-reviewed paper
  • Test type: direct test
  • Tested: In vitro metabolomics of 667 purified E. coli enzymes, analyzed with a machine-learning-derived multivariate classifier, indicated previously unrecognized promiscuous activities in 11% of enzymes tested.
  • Still unknown: The classifier operated at a 33% false-discovery rate; the 135 ion traces were putatively annotated, and only four of 22 reconstructed reaction stoichiometries were experimentally validated. Therefore the full 11% result is a set of candidate activities, not 11% independently confirmed enzyme functions. The RihB activities were prompted by a low-confidence potassium-thymidine-adduct trace and then tested directly with purified enzyme; they should be distinguished from the classifier’s higher-confidence hit set.
  • AI role: A machine-learning-derived multivariate classifier, with a reported false-discovery rate of 33%, detected unexpected changes in metabolite ion traces in the enzyme assays and helped nominate candidate promiscuous activities. The researchers then reconstructed candidate reaction stoichiometries and experimentally validated four reactions.

Evidence sources: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13389410/

12 May 2026Southern University of Science and Technology; Institute of Geomechanics, Chinese Academy of Geological Sciences; ETH Zürich

Machine-learning earthquake catalog reveals scale-dependent fault controls at Gonghe geothermal site

A machine-learning workflow catalogued 7,346 microearthquakes (ML −2.0 to 2.18) recorded during 2021 stimulation and circulation tests at China’s Gonghe enhanced-geothermal-system site. The catalog resolves a ring-shaped distribution with four clusters and varying faulting styles. The authors infer that site-scale seismicity reactivated mapped, pre-existing natural faults; at borehole scale, the principal seismogenic zone coincides with strong SHmax rotation. Stress modeling estimates a low fault-friction coefficient near 0.23 (95% CI 0.19–0.48) and the low-to-moderate fluid overpressure needed for slip.

Technology: Machine-learning earthquake-detection and cataloging workflow (model details are not stated in the publisher abstract)

Unsupervised seismicity categories distinguish documented preparatory phases before three large earthquakes

A K-means framework grouped earthquake families by catalog-derived spatial, temporal, magnitude and seismo-mechanical features. Retrospective analyses found highly localized families with higher interaction and strain release before the 2023 Kahramanmaraş, 2009 L’Aquila and 2014 Iquique earthquakes; similar critical categories were absent before the 2016 Amatrice and 2024 Noto events, where no catalog-visible preparatory phase was detected. The work describes a conditional diagnostic, not a general earthquake prediction system.

Technology: Unsupervised K-means categorization of catalog-derived seismic-family features

CellOracle-guided pancreatic islet differentiation experiments reveal STAT1 and ZEB1 lineage roles

A digital model built from 400,603 cells across 61 single-cell datasets used CellOracle gene-regulatory-network inference and in-silico transcription-factor perturbations to nominate regulators of stem-cell-derived human islet differentiation. CRISPRi experiments supported a previously unreported role for STAT1 in exocrine specification: transient STAT1 knockdown reduced exocrine markers, and JAK–STAT inhibition preserved beta-cell markers and improved glucose-stimulated insulin secretion. CRISPRi also supported a stage-dependent role for ZEB1, whose early knockdown impaired endocrine specification and later knockdown reduced off-target serotonergic cells while increasing beta-cell proportion. The date is the first preprint posting; this entry summarizes the later version reviewed in the research record, which reports the specific STAT1 and ZEB1 experiments.

Technology: CellOracle v0.12.0 within a digital model integrating single-cell transcriptomic and chromatin-accessibility data

20 Mar 2026CMS Collaboration

ParticleNet enables first hadron-collider W-boson mass measurement from hadronic decays

Using 138 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV proton–proton data, CMS reports the first measurement of the W-boson mass in an all-jets final state at a hadron collider: 80.83 ± 0.55 GeV. The result comes from unfolded groomed jet-mass distributions for boosted hadronic W+jets events. The mass-decorrelated ParticleNet graph neural network tagger provides the main result by selecting the W-jet sample and suppressing quark/gluon multijet background; a non-neural N₂ tagger is used as a cross-check.

Technology: ParticleNet mass-decorrelated graph neural network jet tagger

Relevance 47 physics Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

Result, AI contribution and limits

Evidence context (descriptions follow the cited sources; test type is a catalog classification):

  • Publication status: Peer-reviewed paper

  • Tested: Using 138 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV proton–proton data, CMS reports the first measurement of the W-boson mass in an all-jets final state at a hadron collider: 80.83 ± 0.55 GeV.
  • Still unknown: This is an all-jets boosted-W extraction with 0.55 GeV total uncertainty, much less precise than the CMS leptonic-channel W-mass result; the paper frames it as a first step toward future all-jets precision measurements and as a test of jet-substructure modeling. The earlier preliminary CMS result of 80.77 ± 0.57 GeV was superseded by this same paper’s published 80.83 ± 0.55 GeV result and is not counted separately. Jet tagging, QCD background estimation, unfolding, hadronization and jet-energy modeling contribute analysis dependence and uncertainties.
  • AI role: The analysis uses ParticleNet as its main W-jet tagger. Its graph neural network treats jet constituents as an unordered particle cloud and classifies W→qq′ jets against QCD multijet backgrounds; its mass-decorrelated output defines the signal/control regions used for the primary measurement. The N₂ substructure observable is a separate cross-check.

AI-assisted work proves a Latin-square imbalance bound, with optimal examples through order 52

A collaborative LLM-plus-symbolic-computation study proved that every n×n Latin square with n ≡ 1 (mod 3) has imbalance at least 4n(n−1)/9. It introduced near-perfect permutations that attain the bound and computationally found independently verified matching examples for every such order from 4 through 52. The universal lower-bound theorem was formally checked in Lean 4.

Relevance 67 mathematics Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Preprint · Test context: prospective or independent check. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

Result, AI contribution and limits

Evidence context (descriptions follow the cited sources; test type is a catalog classification):

  • Publication status: Preprint
  • Test type: prospective or independent check
  • Tested: A collaborative LLM-plus-symbolic-computation study proved that every n×n Latin square with n ≡ 1 (mod 3) has imbalance at least 4n(n−1)/9.
  • Still unknown: This is an arXiv preprint (v2 dated 2026-08-13), not yet peer-reviewed in the sources checked. The universal proven theorem is a lower bound for n ≡ 1 mod 3. Matching constructions, and hence demonstrated tightness, are computationally established only for n=4,7,…,52; the paper does not prove that the bound is attained for every larger order. Lean 4 formalizes the lower-bound inequality, not the finite construction search or universal tightness.
  • AI role: The agent identified an all-even row-distance parity pattern in numerical search data, formulated and helped prove the lower bound, and used model review to catch proof errors. SageMath and a Rust solver supported symbolic analysis and enumeration; simulated annealing found matching constructions through n=52. Human strategic direction supplied the decisive pivot to the minimum-positive-imbalance question. Lean 4 formally verifies the lower-bound theorem itself.

Evidence sources: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.08322v2

First observation of single-top-quark production with a W and Z boson at CMS

CMS reports the first observation of single-top-quark production in association with a W and Z boson in proton-proton collisions. A Particle Transformer classifier and improved reconstruction separated the rare tWZ signal from major backgrounds in three- and four-lepton events. Combining 13 and 13.6 TeV data (200 fb⁻¹), the measured signal has 5.8σ observed significance (3.5σ expected) and cross sections of 248 ± 52 fb at 13 TeV and 242 ± 77 fb at 13.6 TeV. The result agrees with the Standard Model within 2.3σ.

  • Still unknown: This is the first observation of the Standard-Model tWZ production process, not evidence for physics beyond the Standard Model. A 2024 CMS analysis had reported earlier evidence at 3.4σ; the 2026 paper adds 13.6 TeV Run 3 data and improved reconstruction/ML analysis to reach observation. The 5.8σ result combines 13 and 13.6 TeV datasets. Cross sections and signal strength are consistent with the Standard Model within the reported uncertainties.
  • AI role: CMS trained four ParT models, split by three- versus four-lepton signal region and 13 versus 13.6 TeV samples. In the three-lepton region, a four-node classifier distinguished tWZ, ttZ and other backgrounds; in the four-lepton region, a binary classifier separated tWZ from backgrounds. Its classifier-score categories entered the statistical signal extraction. The paper reports a substantial sensitivity gain versus the previous analysis: expected significance on the reused 13 TeV data rose from 1.4σ to 3.0σ, contributing to the first observation when combined with 13.6 TeV data.

AI-derived histology biomarker stratifies first-line chemotherapy outcomes in advanced pancreatic cancer

The CHAI computational-histology platform generated a locked H&E-based biomarker intended to distinguish advanced pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma patients with differential outcomes on fluoropyrimidine-based versus gemcitabine-based chemotherapy. In an independent validation cohort of 299 patients from the prospectively collected COMPASS and Know Your Tumor cohorts, the 173 patients classified F-pref had longer time to next treatment or death (8.6 vs 7.5 months, P=.035) and overall survival (14.4 vs 11.7 months, P=.003) on F- versus G-based therapy. Result, AI contribution and limits

An earlier CHAI study concerned adjuvant gemcitabine outcomes in resected disease; this entry is limited to the distinct locked first-line fluoropyrimidine-versus-gemcitabine biomarker and external-cohort results in advanced disease.
  • AI role: Deep-learning models segmented H&E biopsy slides and quantified more than 30,000 histomorphologic features. Using the development cohort, the investigators statistically selected and weighted features into a treatment-preference biomarker and locked its threshold before applying it to an independent validation cohort. The platform supplied the image-derived feature measurements used in the biomarker; this is a biomarker-development and validation result, not autonomous treatment assignment.

GPT-5.2 Pro produced the argument and Harmonic's Aristotle a Lean proof of infinitely many triples with a logarithmic gap in a factorial divisibility condition. The arXiv writeup calls it resolved autonomously, which is the author's claim; no independent review is stated.

Technology: GPT-5.2 Pro and Aristotle (Lean)

12 Jan 2026Institut Pasteur de Tunis; Université de Tunis El Manar

Tranylcypromine shows in-vitro activity against Leishmania major

The study experimentally tested the previously model-predicted drug tranylcypromine against L. major promastigotes and intracellular amastigotes. It reports IC50 values of 83.6 and 31.6 µg/mL, respectively, and macrophage CC50 of 282.3 µg/mL. These relatively high in-vitro concentrations do not establish achievable exposure, patient safety or clinical efficacy; human monoamine oxidase mechanism is not shown as the parasite target.

Technology: Prior machine-learning drug-repurposing pipeline (the present study is experimental validation)

DrugCLIP screens about 10,000 human proteins against 500 million compounds

The January 2026 Science abstract reports DrugCLIP screening roughly 10,000 human proteins against 500 million compounds. Experimental hits included 15% for the norepinephrine transporter, with structures of two inhibitor complexes, and 17.5% for TRIP12 using AlphaFold2 structures. Most database results remain computational. The work also has a bioRxiv preprint first indexed in September 2024.

Technology: DrugCLIP (deep contrastive learning)

8 Jan 2026University of Tokyo; Tohoku University; National Research Institute for Earth Science and Disaster Resilience, Japan

Random-forest analysis of continuous seismic waveforms identifies five previously unreported slow-slip events in western Shikoku

A random-forest regression model trained on seismic waveform features predicted GNSS-derived displacement-rate changes over roughly six years in western Shikoku, Japan. Comparing detections with earlier catalogs, the authors report five previously unreported short-term slow-slip events among 23 detected episodes; GNSS deformation patterns and fitted fault models support interpreting the transients as slow slip. The paper-level result is a retrospective detection method and event set, not prospective earthquake prediction.

Technology: Random-forest regression model

Relevance 47 physics Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

Result, AI contribution and limits

Evidence context (descriptions follow the cited sources; test type is a catalog classification):

  • Publication status: Peer-reviewed paper
  • Test type: retrospective or benchmark
  • Tested: A random-forest regression model trained on seismic waveform features predicted GNSS-derived displacement-rate changes over roughly six years in western Shikoku, Japan.
  • Still unknown: The study is retrospective and geographically limited to western Shikoku. Model-predicted rates can differ from observations; smoothing can make events appear longer, a practical threshold affects counts (raising it leaves two newly identified events), and the authors state that events without associated tremor may be missed. It does not establish a prospective earthquake-warning capability or a causal trigger for the event that followed the 2016 Kumamoto earthquake.
  • AI role: Mapped statistical features from continuous seismic waveforms to GNSS-derived displacement rates and flagged sharp predicted increases as possible short-term slow-slip events; authors then fitted fault models and compared deformation with existing event catalogs.

Evidence sources: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s40623-025-02331-5

6 Jan 2026Microsoft Research

CleaveNet designs peptide substrates with MMP13 cleavage profiles

CleaveNet combines a generative model conditioned on protease cleavage profiles with a predictor that ranks candidate sequences. In an in-vitro screen of 95 peptide substrates against 12 matrix metalloproteinases, the authors report that designed substrates were cleaved by MMP13 and identify substrates with different efficiency/selectivity trade-offs. The panel includes training controls and baseline candidates; it is not 95 novel AI discoveries. These are laboratory substrates, not validated diagnostic or therapeutic products.

Technology: CleaveNet generator and predictor; deep learning

5 Jan 2026Stanford University; and collaborating institutions

AI-generated virtual spatial proteomics reveals lung-cancer tumor–immune niches associated with immunotherapy response

HEX, a pathology-image AI model, predicts spatial expression of 40 protein biomarkers from routine H&E slides. In retrospective NSCLC cohorts, combining HEX-derived virtual spatial proteomics with histology improved prognosis prediction and, in a separate 148-patient immune-checkpoint-inhibitor cohort, improved response prediction over H&E-only and virtual-proteomics-only models. The authors interpreted virtual maps as showing co-localized T-helper and cytotoxic T-cell niches among responders and immunosuppressive macrophage/neutrophil aggregates among non-responders.

Technology: HEX (H&E to protein expression), using a pathology foundation-model backbone; MICA (multimodal integration via co-attention)

5 Jan 2026Southeast University Zhongda Hospital; and collaborating clinical and research institutions

A seven-gene machine-learning score shows an Alzheimer-associated signal in an independent plasma cohort

A machine-learning pipeline selected a seven-gene lactylation-related transcriptomic score (LDS) from nine Alzheimer disease cohorts. The study evaluated the signature in seven independent brain transcriptomic datasets and a single-center clinical plasma cohort of 540 participants (180 controls, 90 with amnestic mild cognitive impairment and 270 with Alzheimer disease). Plasma LDS had AUC 0.772 for Alzheimer disease; combining LDS with p-tau181 and p-tau217 had AUC 0.859. LDS scores increased across control, aMCI and Alzheimer groups and correlated with MMSE and Braak stage.

Technology: Lactylation-Derived Score (LDS), a random-forest feature-screening and partial least-squares logistic-regression model

2 Jan 2026Standigm; and Ajou University School of Medicine

Knowledge-graph AI prioritizes TPP1 as a Parkinson’s disease target linked to α-synuclein homeostasis

Standigm ASK’s knowledge-graph model ranked Parkinson’s disease target associations; subgraph enrichment and expression analyses narrowed 2,527 predicted targets to five candidates, including TPP1. In a human cell-based α-synuclein seeding model, TPP1 knockdown increased aggregate accumulation and insoluble α-synuclein, experimentally supporting a TPP1–α-synuclein relationship and a possible protective role.

Technology: Standigm ASK knowledge-graph path-based deep-learning model with subgraph-level over-representation re-ranking

Relevance 53 biology Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

Result, AI contribution and limits

Evidence context (descriptions follow the cited sources; test type is a catalog classification):

  • Publication status: Peer-reviewed paper
  • Test type: direct test
  • Tested: In a human cell-based α-synuclein seeding model, TPP1 knockdown increased aggregate accumulation and insoluble α-synuclein, experimentally supporting a TPP1–α-synuclein relationship and a possible protective role.
  • Still unknown: The functional experiment is a human neuroblastoma cell model exposed to α-synuclein preformed fibrils, not a clinical or in-vivo therapeutic demonstration. Knockdown increasing aggregation supports a protective association; direct enzymatic cleavage of α-synuclein is proposed from structural modeling, not established by the reported work. TPP1 is a candidate therapeutic target, not a validated treatment.
  • AI role: The model integrated heterogeneous biomedical databases, encoded relational paths using a convolutional network and attention aggregation, and produced disease-target scores. Researchers applied enrichment and transcriptomic filters to prioritize TPP1, then validated TPP1’s relationship to α-synuclein aggregation via siRNA knockdown and cellular assays; AlphaFold-Multimer modeling suggested, but did not prove, direct proteolysis.

Evidence sources: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12814083/
